The moving average convergence divergence (MACD) is a technical analysis indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages of a security's price. The MACD is calculated by subtracting the 26-day exponential moving average (EMA) from the 12-day EMA. A buy signal is generated when the MACD crosses above the signal line, which is a 9-day EMA of the MACD. A sell signal is generated when the MACD crosses below the signal line. The MACD is currently above the signal line, which indicates a buy signal.
The relative strength index (RSI) is a technical analysis indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate overbought or oversold conditions in the price of a stock. The RSI is calculated by taking the average gain of the up periods over the past 14 days and dividing it by the average loss of the down periods over the past 14 days. RSI is then plotted as a line between 0 and 100. A reading above 70 indicates that the stock is overbought and may be due for a correction. A reading below 30 indicates that the stock is oversold and may be due for a bounce. The RSI is currently at 65.59, which indicates that the stock is slightly overbought but not yet in overbought territory.
The Fibonacci retracement levels are a set of horizontal lines that are used to identify potential areas of support and resistance. The levels are based on the Fibonacci sequence, which is a series of numbers where each number is the sum of the two preceding numbers. The most common Fibonacci retracement levels are 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. The stock is currently trading near the 61.8% retracement level, which is a potential area of support.
